findings.statement: Nakashima et al. (2005) reported that double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation, so this radiographic sign does not by itself indicate the DTDST-related form of MED.
quotes: Double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.

Reports a four-generation family with EDM2 and a COL9A2 splice-site mutation that segregates with the disease.

findings.statement: Fiedler et al. (2002) described a 4-generation family of 19 individuals, 12 of whom had a variant of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Starting in childhood, the disease caused pain and stiffness of the knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints. Some adult patients had repeated free articular bodies that locked the joint, and affected individuals were prone to early degenerative joint disease. The hips were not markedly affected at an early age.
quotes: We report on a family of 19 individuals over four generations in which 12 members are affected with a variant of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.

Beginning in childhood, the disease leads to pain and stiffness of knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints. Some adult patients repeatedly suffer from free articular bodies resulting in locking of the joint.
Finally, affected individuals are prone to the development of early degenerative joint disease.

phenotypes.text: free articular bodies with joint locking

findings.statement: In the family with EDM2, Fiedler et al. (2002) screened candidate regions and found a new G-to-C change at position -1 of the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splice region, which they thought most likely changes splicing. The change was confirmed by sequencing and by BsaWI digestion in 8 clinically affected family members and in 3 young children who did not yet have symptoms.
quotes: Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region. This G --> C substitution most probably induces an alteration of the splicing process.
We confirmed the nucleotide substitution in eight clinically affected family members as well as in three presymptomatic young children.

variants.as_reported: G-to-C substitution at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region

findings.statement: Fiedler et al. (2002) used electron microscopy on free articular bodies removed by arthroscopy from 2 patients. Collagen fibril diameter was not obviously different from that of normal articular cartilage. Taking previous reports into account, the authors suggested that mutations causing skipping of COL9A2 exon 3, in the COL3 domain of the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen, may be fairly common in the MED subtype in which the hips are not markedly affected early in life (EDM2).
quotes: Electron microscopy showed that the diameter of collagen fibrils from arthroscopically removed free articular bodies of two patients was not obviously different from that of normal articular cartilage.

our results indicate that mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha2-chain of collagen type IX may be relatively common in patients with a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2).

relevance_reason: The title reports that a mutation in COL9A2 causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2), which is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Muragaki et al. (1996) reported that a mutation in the COL9A2 gene, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).
quotes: A mutation in the gene encoding the alpha 2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, COL9A2, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).

relevance_reason: This paper first mapped the EDM2 locus to chromosome 1p, in a region that contains COL9A2. It did so through linkage in a large MED family after the chromosome 19 interval was excluded.

findings.statement: Briggs et al. (1994) studied a large family with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Linkage studies with chromosome 19 markers excluded the interval previously linked to PSACH and to a form of MED. Using this family, the authors identified an MED locus (EDM2) on the short arm of chromosome 1, in a region containing COL9A2. This gene encodes the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen, a structural component of the cartilage extracellular matrix.
quotes: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.
Using this family, we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1, in a region containing the gene (COL9A2) that encodes the alpha 2 chain of type IX collagen

findings.statement: Briggs et al. (1994) excluded the chromosome 19 interval, previously linked to mild and severe PSACH and to a form of MED, in a large MED family that instead mapped to chromosome 1p. This indicated genetic heterogeneity in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
quotes: Recently, both mild and severe PSACH as well as a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19, suggesting that they may be allelic disorders.
Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.

findings.statement: Briggs et al. (1994) described multiple epiphyseal dysplasia as a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis. They noted that some forms clinically resemble mild pseudoachondroplasia.
quotes: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis.
Some forms of MED clinically resemble another chondrodysplasia phenotype, the mild form of pseudoachondroplasia (PSACH).

relevance_reason: Maps the COL9A2 gene, the gene behind EDM2, to human 1p32.3-p33 and mouse chromosome 4. This is gene-mapping background for the disorder entry; the abstract describes no patients.

findings.statement: Warman et al. (1994) mapped the COL9A2 gene, which encodes the alpha-2(IX) collagen chain, to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33 by fluorescence in situ hybridization. Using a single-strand conformational polymorphism within the murine Col9a2 gene, they mapped the mouse gene to chromosome 4.
quotes: COL9A2 was mapped to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33 using fluorescence in situ hybridization.
A single-strand conformational polymorphism within the murine Col9a2 gene was used to map this locus to mouse chromosome 4.

findings.statement: Warman et al. (1994) presented new sequence data that completed the coding sequence of the human alpha-2(IX) collagen chain and revised the chicken sequence. This allowed them to compare the carboxyl-terminal NC1 domains of the alpha-1(IX), alpha-2(IX), and alpha-3(IX) chains across species.
quotes: We also present new sequence data, which completes the coding information for the human alpha 2(IX) chain and revises the sequence for the chicken alpha 2(IX) chain.

relevance_reason: Describes two families with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia complicated by osteochondritis dissecans of the knee, a feature associated with EDM2; abstract only, no gene data.

findings.statement: Versteylen et al. (1988) described 2 families that appeared to contain examples of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Both families had a striking incidence of severe osteochondritis dissecans of the knees. The authors suggested that the osteochondritis was caused by the fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia.
quotes: Two families are described which appear to contain examples of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia.
In both families a striking incidence of severe osteochondritis of the knees was encountered.
It is suggested that this was caused by the fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia.

phenotypes.text: severe osteochondritis dissecans of the knees
